column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/npm-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS PINS. npm-auto-release has three jobs: bump -> {ship |
# publish-withheld}. Four context paths appear in an `if:` — github.actor (the
# bot re-trigger loop guard on bump), needs.bump.outputs.bumped (the publish
# gate), github.event.repository.private and inputs.publish-from-private (the
# privacy guard and its opt-in escape). The table fixes the selected set for
# every combination that can actually occur.
# THE THREE PRIVACY ROWS ARE THE POINT OF THIS FILE, AND ROW 2 REVERSED ON
# 2026-08-17. It used to assert that a PRIVATE repo published anyway, because
# this workflow carried no guard at all and github.event.repository.private
# appeared only inside the two runs-on runner-routing expressions, which select
# a runner and gate nothing. That divergence from cargo-auto-release was
# deliberate-by-accident, and it was a disclosure hole: `npm publish` uploads a
# TARBALL of the package contents to registry.npmjs.org, so a private repo's
# `src` became world-readable, and an npm publish cannot be withdrawn after 72h
# — only deprecated, which withdraws nothing.
# So ship now carries the guard. What makes adding it safe rather than a
# re-run of the very defect the sweep exists to remove is that the guard
# ANNOUNCES ITSELF: publish-withheld is ship's exact complement over the
# bumped case, so exactly one of the two selects whenever a bump happened, and
# a withheld publish emits a ::notice + a step summary instead of an absence.
# Rows 2 and 3 assert both halves of that partition — 2 that a private repo
# withholds AND says so, 3 that the opt-in restores publishing and stands the
# notice down. If either half ever stops holding, the table names it.
# inputs.publish-from-private is declared in EVERY row, including the public
# ones where no `if:` outcome turns on it: an undeclared context path is an
# ERROR by design, because a case that models a scenario while leaving a path
# it does not mention to default silently is how a table drifts out from under
# its workflow. always() and github.event_name are declared for the same
# reason.
# needs-propagation is asserted by row 5: bump is skipped by the bot guard, so
# ship is skipped too even though nothing about ship's own condition changed.
# Its bumped value is EMPTY, not 'false', because that is what a skipped
# upstream job yields — a distinct state the table is able to say.
# publish-withheld skips there on its own condition rather than by propagation
# (its always() lifts it out of the propagation rule on purpose), which is the
# behaviour that keeps the bot loop from emitting a spurious withheld notice.
public-bump
# THE GUARD FIRING, AND SAYING SO. A private repo publishes nothing — and
# publish-withheld runs, so the skip is a statement rather than an absence.
private-bump-withheld
# THE ESCAPE HATCH. A private source deliberately producing a public artifact
# opts in; ship runs and the withheld notice stands down.
private-bump-opt-in
# No version change: bump runs and reports bumped=false; ship is correctly
# gated off, and publish-withheld stays quiet because nothing was withheld —
# there was nothing to publish.
public-no-bump
# Loop guard: the push that bump itself made must not re-enter. bump skips,
# ship skips by needs-propagation (it declares no always()), and
# publish-withheld skips on bumped != 'true' despite its always().
bot-push-loop-guard
